# Incident Report: MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
- **IPv4:** 10.1.21.58
- **MAC:** 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2
- **Windows hostname:** DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (workgroup/domain label WIN11OFFICE, DHCP-confirmed, NBNS-confirmed)
- **Logged-in user:** gwyatt (confirmed via Kerberos CNameString in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic between 10.1.21.58 and the domain controller at 10.1.21.2)
- LAN: 10.1.21.0/24, gateway 10.1.21.2 (MAC 14:b3:1f:2d:ce:69)

## Malware Family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory — only the pcap).

The host is infected with an **HTTP-based information stealer / browser-credential-exfiltration bot**. Behavior consistent with common commodity stealer families (Lumma/StealC-style panels):
- Plaintext HTTP check-in to a `/api/set_agent` endpoint carrying a persistent bot `id` and `token`
- Separate check-ins per installed browser (`agent=Chrome`, then `agent=Edge`), each followed by a `favicon.ico` fetch mimicking normal browser behavior
- A `POST ... &act=log` immediately after each GET, uploading 6.5–8 KB of binary/compressed data per browser (consistent with harvested browser data: cookies, saved credentials, autofill)
- Preceded by a chain of DNS lookups to freshly-registered, fake-file-hosting-style domains (`hiyter.com`, `media.megafilehub4.lat`, `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, `whooptm.cyou`) in the 20 seconds before first C2 contact — consistent with a malvertising/fake-download delivery chain. These sessions were TLS-encrypted, so the delivered payload could not be recovered from the capture (no file object exported, no hash obtainable).

## Indicators of Compromise (all grounded in the capture)

### Command-and-Control
- **153.92.1.49:80** — C2 server, HTTP (confirmed via TLS SNI + plaintext HTTP Host header)
  - Domain: **whitepepper.su**
  - Bot ID: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`
  - Auth token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

### Malicious URLs (observed C2 traffic)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` (POST, 7975 bytes exfiltrated)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log` (POST, 7975 bytes exfiltrated)
- `http://whitepepper.su/favicon.ico` (x2)

### Malicious/suspicious domains (pre-C2 delivery-chain lookups, resolved and visited by the victim, content not recoverable due to TLS)
- `hiyter.com` → 104.21.22.231 / 172.67.207.145
- `media.megafilehub4.lat` → 104.21.48.156 / 172.67.154.67
- `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` → 104.21.46.67 / 172.67.136.13
- `whooptm.cyou` → 62.72.32.156
- `communicationfirewall-security.cc` → 104.21.9.36 / 172.67.141.109 (visited ~24s after C2, possibly a fake-alert/tech-support-scam page)
- `holiday-forever.cc` → 80.97.160.24

**Note:** these six domains are IOCs by association (queried by the infected host shortly before/around C2 activity, all Cloudflare-fronted, no legitimate business purpose observed) but their traffic was TLS-encrypted end to end — no plaintext content, transferred file name, or hash could be extracted from this capture. They should be treated as suspected delivery-chain infrastructure, not confirmed malicious payload servers.

### Transferred files / hashes
**None recoverable.** No executable, script, or archive was transferred in cleartext anywhere in this capture. All non-C2 external sessions besides whitepepper.su were TLS/QUIC-encrypted. The only plaintext HTTP objects exported were the C2 check-in/log bodies above (opaque, likely gzip/encrypted blobs) and benign Microsoft NCSI (`connecttest.txt`) and Google time-sync objects — no SHA256 of a dropped binary can be stated.

## Benign context (not indicators)
- 104.21.46.67, cloudflare-ech.com SNI — generic Encrypted Client Hello placeholder for Cloudflare-fronted sites, largest byte volume in the capture (16 MB) but this reflects the TLS session to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, already listed above.
- Standard Windows/AD chatter: NBNS, LLMNR, CLDAP, Kerberos, DCE/RPC (samr/lsarpc/drsuapi), LDAP to the domain controller (10.1.21.2) — normal enterprise domain-joined workstation activity.
- Microsoft/Google telemetry and services (msn.com, live.com, officeapps, googleapis.com, gstatic.com, bing.com, etc.) — background OS/browser noise.
